Timeline::min¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline Timeline::min(bool skipna = true) const

Find The Earliest Valid Instant¶

min() searches every element and returns the earliest valid timestamp as a scalar Timeline. It is a global reduction: a vector, matrix, or higher-rank Timeline is reduced to shape=[]. There is no dimension argument and no keepdim form.

skipna controls NaT propagation:

  • true (the default) excludes NaT and returns the earliest valid instant.

  • false returns scalar NaT if any input element is NaT.

The comparison uses absolute epoch nanoseconds, not formatted date strings or array position. Input order and duplicate timestamps therefore do not change the result. The receiver is not sorted or mutated.

Absent-Instant Rule¶

With skipna=true, NaT values are skipped while at least one valid timestamp exists. If the Timeline is empty or every element is NaT, min() returns a scalar NaT instead of throwing. This gives the reduction a stable return type, but callers that require a valid result should check isnat_scalar().

Example 1: Reduce A Matrix And Ignore NaT¶

const auto observations = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2025-06-15T08:30:00Z", ""},
    {"2024-01-02T18:45:00Z", "2026-09-30T03:15:00Z"},
});

pluss::timeline::print(std::cout, observations.min());

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[], tz=UTC)
2024-01-02 18:45:00

The earliest value sits in the second row. min() examines the whole matrix; it does not reduce rows independently, and the absent first-row value is not allowed to erase the valid result.

Example 2: Empty And All-NaT Inputs¶

const auto absent = pluss::timeline::make({"", ""});
const auto empty =
    pluss::timeline::from_epoch(std::vector<std::int64_t>{});

pluss::timeline::print(std::cout, absent.min());
std::cout << '\n';
pluss::timeline::print(std::cout, empty.min());

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[], tz=UTC)
NaT
Timeline(shape=[], tz=UTC)
NaT

An empty Timeline has no candidate; an all-NaT Timeline has no valid candidate. Both cases deliberately converge on the same scalar NaT result.

Example 3: Timezone Changes Rendering, Not The Winner¶

const auto utc = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2025-06-15T08:30:00Z",
    "2024-01-02T18:45:00Z",
    "2026-09-30T03:15:00Z",
});
const auto local = utc.tz_convert("America/New_York");

pluss::timeline::print(std::cout, local.min());

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[], tz=America/New_York)
2024-01-02 13:45:00

The selected instant is still 2024-01-02T18:45:00Z; the result simply keeps the receiver’s New York timezone and renders that instant locally.

Example 4: Require A Completely Valid Input¶

const auto observations = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2025-06-15T08:30:00Z", "",
    "2024-01-02T18:45:00Z",
});

pluss::timeline::print(std::cout, observations.min(false));

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[], tz=UTC)
NaT

Use skipna=false when an absent instant should invalidate the reduction instead of being excluded.

Choosing The Right Operation¶

  • Use min() for the earliest timestamp value anywhere in the Timeline.

  • Use argsort() when you need the positions that establish ordering.

  • Use sort() when you need all timestamps arranged chronologically.

  • Do not use min() to obtain the first stored element; chronological minimum and first position are unrelated unless the data is already sorted.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The reduction is global and always returns a scalar Timeline.

  • NaT is ignored by default and propagated when skipna=false.

  • Ties do not expose which occurrence won because the method returns a value, not an index.

  • The default Timeline printer displays whole seconds; the stored timestamp and comparison retain nanosecond precision.

Summary¶

min() means “earliest valid instant over all elements.” It preserves temporal type and timezone, skips NaT by default, can propagate it on request, returns scalar NaT when no valid candidate exists, and never changes the receiver.

See Also¶

  • max: return the latest valid instant.

  • argsort: obtain chronological positions.

  • isnat_scalar: validate the scalar result.
